title: ESpma: A method for assessing biological/non-biological interfaces using point-clouds-based structural features and protein language models.
authors: Nozawa, Sarah; Tomii, Kentaro; Fukasawa, Yoshinori
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
one_liner_zh: 该文利用蛋白语言模型嵌入的界面局部池化与点云结构特征，开发了区分生物/非生物蛋白界面的轻量级方法，属于蛋白质结构相关的计算建模任务，但方法创新性有限且性能未显著超越现有方法。
abstract: Distinguishing biological protein-protein interfaces from non-biological contacts remains an important task in structural biology, particularly as protein complex structures continue to accumulate. Recent advances in protein language models (pLMs) have expanded their use across diverse protein prediction tasks, including sequence-based protein-protein interaction prediction. Such approaches often pool representations over entire sequences, whereas structure-based methods commonly rely on more complex graph- or geometry-based integration. We therefore asked how much interface-relevant information could be extracted by simply pooling pLM embeddings over structurally defined local regions. Here, we revisited biological-versus-crystal interface classification as a structurally well-defined testbed for this question. We developed a framework that compares full-sequence pooling, interface-localized pooling of pLM embeddings, and multimodal integration of sequence-derived embeddings with point-cloud representations of protein surfaces. On two benchmark datasets, interface-localized pooling achieved stronger performance than full-sequence or non-interacting surface pooling across three pLM backbones. Despite its simplicity, the resulting representation performed within the range of established methods that rely on explicit evolutionary analysis or geometric modeling. Incorporating explicit geometric surface information changed performance slightly, without reaching statistical significance. Because the model is linear, the interface-level score decomposes exactly into per-residue contributions, which varied within amino-acid types. Together, our results indicate that the principal gain arises from localizing pLM embeddings to physically interacting residues, enabling a lightweight and accessible implementation for biological-versus-crystal interface classification. Code and scripts are available on GitHub: https://github.com/fukasawa-group/espma.
abstract_zh: 区分生物性蛋白质-蛋白质界面与非生物性接触仍是结构生物学中的一项重要任务，尤其是在蛋白质复合物结构持续积累的背景下。蛋白质语言模型（pLMs）的最新进展已将其应用扩展到多种蛋白质预测任务，包括基于序列的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用预测。此类方法通常对整个序列的表征进行池化，而基于结构的方法则常依赖更复杂的图或几何集成。因此，我们探究了通过简单地对结构定义的局部区域上的pLM嵌入进行池化，能提取多少界面相关信息。在此，我们将生物性-晶体界面分类重新审视为一个结构上明确定义的测试平台，以回答这一问题。我们开发了一个框架，比较了全序列池化、界面局部池化pLM嵌入，以及序列衍生嵌入与蛋白质表面点云表征的多模态集成。在两个基准数据集上，界面局部池化在三种pLM骨干网络中均实现了比全序列或非相互作用表面池化更强的性能。尽管其简单性，所得表征的性能处于依赖显式进化分析或几何建模的既有方法范围内。引入显式几何表面信息仅轻微改变性能，未达到统计显著性。由于模型是线性的，界面级分数可精确分解为每个残基的贡献，这些贡献在氨基酸类型间有所变化。综合来看，我们的结果表明，主要增益源于将pLM嵌入定位到物理相互作用的残基上，从而为生物性-晶体界面分类提供了一种轻量且易于实现的方案。代码和脚本可在GitHub上获取：https://github.com/fukasawa-group/espma。
